Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

accompany verb

also go with, come with, escort, see someone home, see someone off, walk someone home, accompanied by

classical

Suet. Gram. 23: erīlem fīlium in scholās (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 9.21: adultōs diū comitantur

comitor, comitārī, comitātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent, transitive

accompany, go with, attend

With the accusative; classical, but most frequent after the Augustan period (Lewis & Short). “Accompanied by” is the ablative absolute: magnā comitante catervā (Verg. A. 2.40), or with the noun comes, asellō comite (Phaedr. 1.11.3). “Go with someone” is also simply cum aliquō īre (see with).

Other words

  • prōsequor, prōsequī, prōsecūtus sum — go along with, see off, escort

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 4.2.3: novum marītum volō rūs prōsequī (Lewis & Short); Ov. Tr. 1.8.14: exsequiās (Lewis & Short)

    Following someone out as an escort or in his honour: seeing him off, attending a funeral (exsequiās prōsequī). It also means to pursue an enemy, and to honour someone with words or gifts (Lewis & Short).

  • dēdūcō, dēdūcere, dēdūxī, dēductum — escort (someone from his house)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 63: dēdūcī, redūcī; Cic. Fam. 10.12.2 (Lewis & Short)

    “A term of common life” (Lewis & Short): to escort a person out of his house as a mark of respect or for protection; redūcere is to see him home again. Its general sense is “lead away, bring down”; of a bride, to bring her to her husband’s house.

Examples

  • vēnārī asellō comite cum vellet leō

    when the lion wanted to go hunting with the donkey for companyPhaedr. 1.11.3

  • quīn et adultōs diū comitantur magnā ergā partum cāritāte

    indeed they stay with their young long after they are grown, so great is their love for their offspringPlin. NH 9.21

  • haec enim ipsa sunt honōrābilia quae videntur levia atque commūnia, salūtārī, adpetī, dēcēdī, adsurgī, dēdūcī, redūcī, cōnsulī

    for these very things that seem slight and ordinary are marks of honour: to be greeted, sought out, made way for, stood up for, escorted from home and back, consultedCic. Sen. 63

See also with, company, together, meet.

SourcesLewis & Short: comitor · Lewis & Short: prosequor · Lewis & Short: deduco
